## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D FPS/third-person shooter with real players or bots.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots (viewport at most 1280px wide) for visual checks and inspect only the latest.

## Decisions
- Implemented a single-player free-for-all training simulation with five AI bots; no network multiplayer was added.
- Built the game as a standalone Three.js page with responsive mobile touch controls.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added arena, first-/third-person views, bot AI and combat, HUD, minimap, match timer, pause/restart, and mobile controls in `index.html`.
- Started a local HTTP server on port 3002 and checked the menu in Chromium.
- Fixed a startup error (`ReferenceError: Cannot access 'skinMat' before initialization`) and confirmed the page reloads without console errors.

### Active
- Validate gameplay in-browser, not just the menu; inspect for runtime errors and capture a latest JPEG after deploying.

### Blocked
- Real-player online multiplayer is not implemented.

## Next Move
1. Click “DEPLOY TO THE ARENA” and verify movement, shooting, bot behavior, pause/restart, and view switching.
2. Save and inspect a current gameplay screenshot under `screenshots/`.
3. Report the single-player/bot scope and any remaining issues.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete game implementation.
- `screenshots/menu.jpg`: Latest menu screenshot.
- `README.md`: Existing project landing-page content.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Local server is running at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Playwright browser is open; first browser load logged the fixed `skinMat` initialization error, but the subsequent reload reported zero console errors.
